Yes, that is true at the federal level in Switzerland. A federal popular initiative can indeed propose the introduction of new federal laws or amendments to existing ones. This is one of the forms of direct democracy available to Swiss citizens at the federal level, alongside the optional referendum. Swiss citizens have the constitutional right to propose amendments to the Federal Constitution through an initiative.

However, it is important to note that not all cantons have the same provisions. While some cantons do allow popular initiatives to propose new laws or amendments within the cantonal legal framework, the federal system explicitly provides this right at the national level. The federal popular initiative is a powerful instrument that allows citizens to directly influence federal legislation and constitutional amendments.
